newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity closes lower in line with natgas.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity closes lower in line with natgas.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures closed sharply lower in line with weaker natural gas prices spurred by warmer weather, trade sources said Monday.
"Early in the morning sellers came in fairly aggressively," said one trader.
Market sources also cited ample hydroelectric supplies in the Northwest as putting downward pressure on power prices.
One trader noted many players seem to have flattened their positions after today's volatility ahead of Christmas.
NYMEX will hold a half-day session Tuesday, closing trade in all its energy contracts at 1300 EST for Christmas Eve.
The exchange will be shut Wednesday for Christmas Day.
"People are wrapping things up. Outside of some crazy move in the gas market things should be pretty quiet the rest of the week," said another trader.
January electricity contracts will expire on Thursday, while NYMEX January natgas expires Tuesday.

January 1997 California-Oregon border (COB) futures closed down $3.80 at $23.05 per megawatt hour (MWh), while the February contract was down $1.60 at $18.50. Other active COB contracts lost 50 to 65 cents.
January Palo Verde was down $3.42 at $24.26 per MWh, while February was down $2.25 at $19.50. Other PV contracts were down 50 cents to $1.50.
